answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it votes on work or claims rewards. The protocol caps each deposit’s influence, then slashes it when an identity is proven to have double-voted or submitted fraudulent results. Creating a hundred identities no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital in every one and risks losing it. This prevents a sybil spiral from cheaply capturing the harbor, while leaving honest agents free to join the reef.
